data.description:
# Make the GENERATED doc/config surfaces discoverable, so plans stop citing derived files

## Context / Problem

Story 316a (`common-middle-yearling`) needed FOUR CI iterations to land, and three of the four
failures had the same root cause: the plan cited a **derived** file by line number, so the
implementer edited the generated artifact instead of its source, and a drift gate failed.

The surfaces that bit it, none of which announce themselves as generated at the point an author
would look:

1. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` - derived from the prompt front-matter; regenerate with
   `python -m rebar.llm.prompting.prompts regenerate-index`. Gate: "Prompt-index drift gate".
2. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md` front-matter - must be a FIXED POINT of `write_front_matter()`
   (`write(*split_raw(f)) == f`). Semantically-correct YAML wrapped by hand still fails.
   Gate: `tests/unit/test_prompt_front_matter.py::test_built_in_prompt_round_trips_canonically`.
3. `docs/cli-reference.md` - derived from the CLI help data + a curated table in
   `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`. Gate: "CLI-reference drift gate".
4. `docs/mcp-reference.md` - derived from the MCP tool docstrings via
   `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`. Gate: "MCP-reference drift gate".

`docs/env-vars.md` and the public-types output are in the same family. By contrast
`docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/output-schemas.md` and `AGENTS.md` ARE hand-authored - and nothing
distinguishes the two groups when you open them.

The cost is real and repeatable: each wrong edit burns a full CI round-trip (10+ minutes of
runner time plus a Verified -1), and the drift gates run late in the pytest job's pre-suite
sequence, so a single stale derived file masks every gate behind it and the suite never runs.

## Approach

Two cheap, independent moves; either is useful alone.

**1. Make the file say so.** Add a generated-by banner as the first line of each derived doc
(`<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py - do not edit; regenerate instead -->`) and an
equivalent comment where the format allows it. An author who opens the file to edit line 478 sees
it immediately. JSON has no comment syntax, so `index.json` instead gets a `"_generated_by"` key
(the loader must ignore unknown top-level keys, or the key must be added to its schema).

**2. Make the docs say so.** Add a short "Generated artifacts" section to `docs/README.md`
listing each derived surface, its SOURCE, its regenerate command, and the CI gate that enforces
it - one table. Point `CONTRIBUTING.md` at it from the commit checklist.

Optionally (decide during implementation, do not assume): a single
`make regen` target that runs every generator, so a contributor does not have to know which of
the six commands applies.

## Scope

- `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`, `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`,
  `rebar.llm.prompting.prompts regenerate-index` - each emits its banner.
- The regenerated outputs themselves.
- `docs/README.md` - the new table.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` - one pointer line.
- Possibly `Makefile` for the aggregate target.

## Testing

- A unit test asserting every file listed in the new `docs/README.md` table carries its banner AND
  is a fixed point of its generator - so the table cannot go stale, which is the failure mode this
  ticket is fixing one level up.
- Re-run each existing drift gate; all must stay green with the banners present.
- Confirm `index.json`'s loader tolerates the `_generated_by` key (add a case that round-trips it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/mcp-reference.md` and `docs/env-vars.md` opens with a
      banner naming its generator script; verified by `head -1` on each file.
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` carries a `_generated_by` value naming the regenerate
      command, and loading the catalog still works; verified by the existing prompt/catalog suites
      staying green.
- [ ] `docs/README.md` contains a table with one row per generated surface giving source,
      regenerate command, and enforcing CI gate; verified by reading it and by the new test below.
- [ ] A test fails if a file listed in that table lacks its banner or is not a fixed point of its
      generator; verified by planting a stale file locally and seeing the test go red.
- [ ] Every existing drift gate still passes with the banners in place; verified by running the
      pytest job's pre-suite gate sequence locally (prompt-index, env-registry, CLI-reference,
      MCP-reference, docs-index, README quickstart).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
data.title: Mark the generated doc/config surfaces as generated
